title: Contain prompt-asset failures across CLI paths
description:
## Objective
Convert missing/malformed prompt asset errors into exit-1 failed results with logical-asset and reinstall guidance on both flag-driven and zero-argument wizard paths, without breaking non-rendering recovery commands.

## Context
The loader fails closed, but current flag-driven error handling always advises Paseo connectivity and the wizard runs outside that boundary. REQ-005 requires actionable contained failure rather than an unhandled rejection or incomplete document.

## Scope
In scope:
- Add/consume a dedicated prompt-asset error signal from `src/room/prompts.ts`.
- Restructure `src/cli.ts` so wizard and parsed-command execution share appropriate thrown-error containment.
- Preserve the generic Paseo-connectivity fix for unrelated failures; use reinstall guidance only for prompt assets.
- Add tests for flag-driven and wizard paths plus a non-rendering recovery path.
Out of scope:
- Broad CLI diagnostic rewrite, new flags/commands, carrier changes, or package tests.

## Components Touched
- `src/room/prompts.ts` — error metadata/type if not already complete.
- `src/cli.ts` — common error boundary and error-specific fix mapping.
- `src/wizard.ts` only if required to expose the same result boundary without changing UX.
- CLI/wizard tests — missing and malformed asset behavior.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- `Remove legacy prompt sources and migration fixtures` must complete so tests target the final loader/renderer.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Both paths return exit 1 and emit a normal failed result; no raw stack/unhandled rejection.
- Error names the logical asset and advises reinstalling `paseo-room`.
- Lazy loading keeps `remove` and other non-rendering recovery behavior available.
- Do not alter auth guidance or ordinary operator diagnostics.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Moving the wizard into a catch must not swallow Commander help/version exits or change no-command non-TTY exit 2 behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Missing/malformed asset tests pass for flag-driven and wizard execution with exit 1, asset name, and reinstall fix.
- No unhandled rejection occurs.
- Generic non-asset failures retain current guidance and parsing/help behavior.
- A non-rendering recovery command does not read prompt assets.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and focused CLI tests pass.

## Primary Proof
Focused CLI/wizard negative tests covering both error classes and unaffected recovery/parsing paths.

## Reversibility
Restore the prior CLI branch/catch structure and error mapping; the prompt loader and generated state remain unchanged.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/role-contract-markdown-implementation-plan.md#WP-002
Requirements: REQ-005, REQ-007
Design refs: docs/design/role-contract-markdown.md §§3.2, 4.1, 6
close_reason: Contained PromptAssetError on scripted and zero-argument wizard paths as exit-1 failed results with logical-asset/reinstall guidance, while preserving generic connectivity errors, help/version/non-TTY parsing, and lazy non-rendering remove. title: Execute locked filesystem and Paseo provider transactions
description:
## Objective
Compose planned file operations and one three-provider daemon patch under a deterministic per-user daemon/provider lock, with verification, manifest commit, and reverse compensation.

## Context
Different room roots and endpoint aliases target the same provider IDs; only one can claim them, and filesystem plus daemon changes are not ACID.

## Scope
In scope:
- Global `/tmp/paseo-room-<uid>` lock, stale-owner validation, local-admission recheck, active-session refusal, transaction state machine, provider patch/read-back/refresh, manifest commit.
Out of scope:
- Interrupted-journal recovery UI and partial uninstall cleanup.

## Components Touched
- Transaction orchestrator, lock implementation, Paseo gateway integration, manifest writer, concurrency tests.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Private journal/file primitives and live Paseo provider verification must exist.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Lock key is SHA-256 of canonical local Paseo home, normalized status listen endpoint, and fixed provider namespace only; room root, endpoint spelling, TMPDIR, and XDG variables cannot split it.
- Re-read local home/PID/UID/listen admission and current providers after lock. Refuse non-terminal managed sessions. No automatic mutation retry.
- Install/update commit is atomic manifest with matching transaction ID; failed verification compensates conditionally.

## Risks / Gotchas
- External same-ID writers are unsupported; visible divergence must become recovery-required, never trigger whole-config restore.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Two processes using distinct roots, endpoint aliases, and environment paths admit exactly one provider owner.
- Injected failures around daemon patch/refresh/verify/manifest commit reach old committed, new committed, or recovery-required state.
- Successful apply creates exactly three ready profiles and second apply performs no mutation.

## Primary Proof
Concurrency plus cross-filesystem/daemon fault-injection integration suite using fakes and isolated daemon.

## Reversibility
Before-values and file before-images compensate only owned after-values; divergence remains preserved with journal evidence under the R3 containment policy.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-room-phase-1-implementation-plan.md#wp-005-transaction-global-lock-rollback-and-recovery
Requirements: REQ-003, REQ-006, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-014
Design refs: docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#72-apply-and-rollback-flow; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#73-locking-and-idempotency; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#r3-decision
notes: DONE 2026-09-09: Added deterministic owner-only global lock keyed solely by canonical Paseo home, normalized loopback listen and fixed provider namespace; PID/start evidence fails closed for busy/stale/unsafe ownership. Added journal-bound no-clobber manifest commit, transaction orchestrator, public-SDK transaction gateway and committed cleanup. Executor rechecks admission/providers/sessions under lock, publishes files, issues one complete patch, performs full readback/refresh/readiness/policy/file verification, and commits a same-ID manifest. Conditional reversal preserves unrelated/divergent providers/files; unresolved forward/reverse RPCs and failed restored-registry verification retain recovery evidence. R2 findings remediated; final independent review PASS. Verified npm run verify: typecheck, lint, 17 files/1022 tests, build, pack and package test. Isolated Paseo 0.8.0-beta.1 contract: 2/2 unauthenticated/authenticated cases passed. Cross-process lock proof uses an acquisition barrier and distinct room roots/endpoint spelling/TMPDIR/XDG.
close_reason: DoD verified: locked end-to-end install/update transaction, crash-safe manifest commit, conditional compensation, concurrency proof, R2 PASS, full and isolated gates green

title: Migrate prompt prose to semantic Markdown rendering
description:
## Objective
Introduce the canonical Markdown asset tree, lazy validated synchronous loader, typed semantic manifest, and semantic renderer; switch production composition and forced test consumers while preserving all non-heading bytes and role distribution.

## Context
The accepted design uses one Markdown file per independently distributed section, document head, and Pi capsule. Runtime reads assets relative to `import.meta.url`, validates shape, memoizes successful reads, and renders semantic headings without a Markdown parser.

## Scope
In scope:
- Create every `src/room/prompts/**` asset listed in Technical Design §2.2.
- Add `src/room/prompts.ts` with typed path/kind manifest, lazy `readFileSync`, shape validation, section normalization, `trimEnd()` handling for heads/capsules, successful-read caching, and actionable prompt-asset errors.
- Replace numeric composition in `src/room/instructions.ts` with ordered semantic keys and rename repository helpers to `instructionKeys()` / `protocolKeys()`.
- Source Pi communication/runtime capsules from canonical Markdown while preserving outer ordering.
- Update forced imports/assertions in `test/instructions.test.ts`, `test/cli.test.ts`, `test/codex.test.ts`, `test/claude.test.ts`, and `test/pi.test.ts`.
- Run the transitional legacy-vs-Markdown comparison.
Out of scope:
- Deleting legacy prose files/fixtures; the cleanup bead owns that.
- CLI catch/wizard containment changes.
- Build copying, package tests, docs, wording, or authority changes.

## Components Touched
- `src/room/prompts/**` — canonical prose assets.
- `src/room/prompts.ts` — loader, manifest, error, validation, cache.
- `src/room/instructions.ts` — semantic ordered composition.
- `src/room/clauses.ts`, `src/room/workspace.ts` — retained temporarily only as comparison inputs.
- `src/agents/pi.ts` — canonical capsule consumption.
- Prompt/carrier tests named above — semantic key and heading assertions.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- `Establish temporary legacy-render characterization evidence` must be complete so the migration has byte-preservation proof.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- One file per semantic section; exact paths/headings come from Technical Design §§2.2 and 7.
- Contract/workspace statements use blank-line boundaries and collapse wrapped lines; H2-to-first-bullet is one newline.
- Document heads/Pi capsules preserve internal hard lines after `trimEnd()`; renderer owns inter-fragment separators/final newline.
- Numeric IDs are not active keys or rendered headings; semantic keys are implementation-only.
- Loader failures are not cached; no source-checkout fallback or new dependency.

## Risks / Gotchas
- `Challenge Signals` appears in different ordered positions for Lead and Peer; Peer must still omit Topology and orchestration/seat-creation content.
- Lazy loading is required so non-rendering recovery commands do not fail on absent assets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Transitional comparison proves only accepted headings changed across all documents/Pi append.
- Manifest/filesystem bijection and fragment shape tests pass.
- Exact semantic heading sequences and role/workspace distribution tests pass, including Peer negatives.
- Repeated renders are byte-identical; Pi outer order is unchanged.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm test` pass while legacy comparison sources remain available.

## Primary Proof

## Reversibility
Before downstream work, restore the legacy imports/renderer and remove the new asset tree/loader; no installed room or credential state is modified.

title: Plan deterministic install, update, verify, and uninstall operations
description:
## Objective

## Context

- Property tests preserve random unrelated providers and prove normalized operation ordering/idempotency.

description:
## Objective
Add a dedicated offline package-test suite and make it the final step of `npm run verify`, proving complete packed role/workspace rendering and actionable failure when one installed asset is missing.

- Add `test:package` and append it after build in `npm run verify`.
- Use fake Paseo/Codex binaries, valid fixture Codex config, isolated `$HOME`, and an ephemeral loopback port closed before execution.

title: Implement private staging, journal, and atomic file mutation primitives
description:
## Objective
Implement secure transaction staging, before-image capture, fsynced journal transitions, atomic per-file publish, and conditional filesystem compensation.

## Context
Filesystem changes precede provider activation but span multiple files, so every mutation needs durable intent/evidence and safe reverse behavior after handled errors or interruption.

## Scope
In scope:
- `src/core/transaction.ts` filesystem/journal primitives, private directories/files, atomic rename/fsync, file/link before/after records, and injectable faults.
Out of scope:
- Paseo patch orchestration, global lock, and command UX.

## Components Touched
- Transaction/journal/filesystem modules and failure-injection fixtures.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Deterministic planner and manifest ownership models must exist.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Roots/backups/staging are 0700; regular files/journals are 0600. Never follow links or recursively replace role containers.
- Journal is persisted before mutation and after each completed step. Atomicity is per file only.
- Compensation restores only when current still equals transaction after-value; divergence is preserved.

## Risks / Gotchas
- SIGKILL/power loss cannot run handlers; durable journal must make the state classifiable later.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Fault injection around every file mutation yields restored old state or explicit divergent recovery state.
- Modes, fsync/rename sequencing, link metadata backup, and no credential dereference are tested.
- SIGINT/SIGTERM handler path invokes conditional compensation.

## Primary Proof
Exhaustive temporary-filesystem journal/fault matrix across every state transition.

## Reversibility
All tests use disposable roots; production primitives retain before-images and never overwrite divergence.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-room-phase-1-implementation-plan.md#wp-005-transaction-global-lock-rollback-and-recovery
Requirements: REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-014, REQ-016

title: Wire the non-interactive lifecycle command surface
description:
## Objective
Implement `plan`, `install`, `verify`, `doctor`, `recover`, and `uninstall` command routing, automation flags, human/JSON results, and exact exit codes over the shared lifecycle services.

## Context
CI and operators need deterministic commands where dry-run is default and mutation authorization is centralized.

## Scope
In scope:
- Commander command definitions, flag precedence/validation, service composition, renderers, diagnostics, and exit mapping.
- `--agent codex`, `--apply`, `--json`, `--non-interactive`, and documented path/binary/url options.
Out of scope:

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Transaction, recovery, planner, Codex adapter, and Paseo gateway outcomes must be complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Without `--apply`, install/recover/uninstall are read-only plans. Non-interactive mode never prompts.
- JSON stdout is one schema-v1 document; secrets never appear. Exit codes are 0 success, 1 failure, 2 usage, 3 conflict, 4 recovery-required.
- CLI does not install/start/stop/upgrade Paseo or Codex.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Black-box tests cover every command/outcome/exit code and missing input.
- Filesystem/gateway spies prove only explicit `--apply` reaches mutation.
- Human diagnostics are actionable and JSON output is deterministic and uncontaminated.

Packed/unpacked non-interactive CLI golden and mutation-authorization tests.

CLI wiring is repository-local; all mutation tests use disposable state with transaction rollback.

title: Make managed replacement type-safe and atomic
description:
## Objective
Make managed file/link replacement type-safe and atomic, and add an exact managed-directory primitive limited to generated Peer skill projections.

## Context
Current apply removes paths recursively before writing. Peer skill filtering also needs a bounded migration from a legacy directory symlink and exact stale-child reconciliation without transaction machinery.

## Scope
In scope:
- Refuse unexpected path types before deletion.
- Replace regular files and symlinks through unique sibling temporaries and rename; clean temporaries on failure.
- Add an exact managed-directory entry that may migrate the known legacy symlink and reconcile declared child names only.
- Add focused filesystem tests.
Out of scope:
- Transactions, rollback journals, locks, exact reconciliation of role homes, credential paths, or arbitrary directories.

## Components Touched
- src/fsops.ts — Entry model, planning, apply behavior.
- test filesystem/unit files — type refusal, atomic replacement, cleanup, managed-directory migration/reconciliation.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- None.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- macOS/Linux and Node 22 are the supported platforms.
- Credential paths never become managed entries.
- Recovery remains rerun setup.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Never recursively delete an unexpected real directory.
- Exact managed-directory ownership must be explicit in the Entry type and cannot be inferred from an ordinary dir.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Unexpected directory/file/symlink shapes are preserved and fail actionably.
- Existing regular files/symlinks update and remain idempotent.
- Temporary siblings do not remain after success/failure.
- Managed directory migrates only the declared legacy symlink and removes only stale declared children.

## Primary Proof
Focused fsops and CLI filesystem tests, then typecheck.

## Reversibility
Revert the Entry/apply primitive and tests; no persistent data outside generated room paths changes.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/orchestration-quality-hardening-implementation-plan.md#WP-005
Requirements: C11; WP-002 filesystem prerequisite
Design refs: docs/design/orchestration-quality-hardening.md#d7--managed-replacement-safety


## Acceptance Criteria
